display_name: Four jurisdictions, one ontology — unilateral mistake compared against Singapore's equitable limb
modules_note: Listed in dependency order. mistake-domain declares the shared vocabulary the four jurisdiction modules import; mistake-comparison holds the machinery for reading their verdicts side by side and owns the one consequence -- what a verdict does to a third party -- that belongs to no single jurisdiction; mistake-cases holds every fixture and every assertion. No jurisdiction module imports another, by design: a comparison in which one test could read another's answer would not be a comparison.
scope: The Singapore doctrine of unilateral mistake in contract, at common law and in equity, as stated in Chwee Kin Keong v Digilandmall.com Pte Ltd [2005] SGCA 2 and restated in Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd [2020] SGCA(I) 02, encoded alongside three comparators so that what is distinctive about it can be measured rather than asserted. The comparators are NOT independent surveys of their jurisdictions: each is one authority read through Chwee Kin Keong's account of it, except the American module, which is the Restatement rule quoted from a Californian judgment. See subject.json's authority_note and NOTES.md section 3.
assertions_note: MEASURED 2026-09-07 with `l4 run mistake-cases.l4`: 69 #ASSERT directives, 69 satisfied, 0 failed, 0 errors. Four of the 69 are `#ASSERT REFUSED`, which assert that the England module declines to answer. The run transcript is tests/run-transcript.txt. Note that `l4 run` prints every result twice -- once in diagnostics, once as an Evaluation block -- so a reader counting `assertion satisfied` in the transcript will find 138.
versions_encoded: Singapore law as stated in Chwee Kin Keong (13 January 2005), as restated in Quoine (24 February 2020). No rule-version axis and no dated arms: the encoding cannot answer about the law before 2005.

not_reviewed.note: No human review has been sought, and no pipeline run stands behind this row -- there is no etc/go sidecar for this subject, so there are no receipts, no journal and no waiver. What HG1 would ask of a reviewer is a domain expert reading each module against the judgment it cites, paragraph by paragraph, and the characterisation of each fixture against the facts as found. NOTES.md section 6 lists the specific things such a reviewer should attack first.
